title: Launch cadence synchronization hub for runtime, console, and API
creator: Aisha Park
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable launch cadence "synchronization hub" and communication pattern to coordinate simultaneous and staggered launches across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. The hub will standardize kickoff steps, pre-launch gating metrics, dependency matrices, and a single cross-team calendar to minimize conflicts and improve predictability for customers and enterprise sales.
background: We have frequent mismatches between runtime feature availability, console rollout readiness, and API compatibility windows. This results in last-minute rollbacks, unclear customer messaging, and overloaded on-call. Current artifacts are ad hoc: per-project timelines in Google Sheets, Slack-based escalations, and inconsistent canary percentages. We need a consistent orchestration layer in our launch process that lives with Product and is operationalized by PM/ENG/Design leads.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical cross-surface launch calendar (Google Calendar + read-only Confluence view) for all planned launches through Q2 2026
A 6-step pre-launch checklist agreed by Runtime, Console, API, SRE, and Solutions SEs and stored as a template in Confluence
Gating metric definitions for canary progression: latency P95, error rate, request throughput, cost delta, and customer regression score
A go/no-go decision rubric and escalation path documented and validated in a dry-run for the next minor release
Mapping of capacity reservations for Dedicated customers with a two-week buffer to avoid contention
tasks: Define hub governance and rotating coordinator role (PM-led, 4-week rotations)
Build calendar + view in Confluence; create read-only calendar for external stakeholders
Draft pre-launch checklist and gating metric thresholds with ENG/SRE/QA
Add a lightweight Slack + PagerDuty escalation playbook and channel naming convention
Run one practice synchronization for runtime-2.4 minor release in March
Create template PRD/launch summary that each surface must publish three weeks prior to launch
stakeholders: ENG: Priya Shah (Runtime), Omar Velasquez (API), Mei Tan (Console)
timeline: Feb 2026: governance and checklist. Mar 2026: calendar + Confluence view, Slack playbook, dry-run with runtime-2.4. Apr 2026: iterate and roll out to Dedicated onboarding flows.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams ignore central calendar leading to drift -> Mitigation: route mandatory pre-launch milestone approvals through the hub coordinator; add calendar check to sprint gating
Risk: Capacity contention for Dedicated pools -> Mitigation: require Dedicated capacity reservation two weeks before launch and surface conflicts in weekly sync
Risk: Gating thresholds too conservative and block good launches -> Mitigation: baseline thresholds off last 4 release windows and include a tuning feedback loop after each release
decisions: Adopt a rotating PM coordinator rather than a centralized release manager to keep overhead low
Use existing Google Calendar and Confluence rather than building a custom tool for Q2 rollout
Require a single line item in each release PRD documenting rollback plan and SLA exposure
